scope: Published Scottish town tourist-appeal ratings after source-backed top-places expansion.

ratingScale.0: Not a tourist town: local services or minor heritage only, with no strong reason for tourists to visit specifically.
ratingScale.1: Niche detour: one or two genuine visitor draws, usually worthwhile only if nearby or already interested in the theme.
ratingScale.2: Worth a planned stop: several credible attractions or a strong town story, but not destination-level on its own.
ratingScale.3: Destination draw: nationally recognisable or dense visitor appeal that can anchor an itinerary.

decisions.reason: UNESCO Forth Bridge setting, Forth Bridges Trail, bridge viewpoints, boat trips, museum, waterfront High Street and Port Edgar are strong enough for destination-level appeal.

Polygon-only sweep excludes Polkemmet Country Park and the Scottish Owl Centre because both mapped visitor points sit outside the Whitburn polygon; without them Whitburn remains local-service/heritage context rather than a tourist town.
Palace, loch and Peel, St Michael's, museum, canal centre and historic town setting justify destination-level appeal.
Preserved royal burgh, palace, abbey, town house, Mercat Cross and West Kirk are enough for a destination draw.

Falls of Dochart, Bridge of Dochart and Finlarig Castle are all inside the polygon and still sustain a destination rating; out-of-polygon Clan MacNab and stone-circle stops are no longer counted as top highlights.

J M Barrie's Birthplace, Peter Pan, Bon Scott and Gateway to the Glens are inside the polygon and still make it worth a planned stop; Camera Obscura is no longer counted because its point is outside the polygon.
Museums, gasworks, church, Corn Exchange and puppet-theatre context justify a planned stop; the puppet theatre still needs a clean map point before it is added to highlights.
Alloa Tower is strong, but the wider visitor offer remains a niche heritage detour rather than a broad tourist town.
Alva Glen and Silver Glen support a good short nature/heritage detour, not a standalone town destination.
St Serf's Church and the Dupplin Cross are a genuine specialist stop, but the offer is compact.
Outdoor pool, Clyde views, ferry/pier and Kempock Stone support a pleasant detour, but not a destination rating.
Almond Valley, shale museum and shopping are real visitor uses, but the town is still not primarily a tourist destination.
Torphichen Preceptory is a genuine specialist medieval stop, but the broader village offer is limited.
Sterling Mills, Tillicoultry Glen and Devon Way improve the visitor case but remain a nearby/niche detour rather than a destination.
Specialist planned-village heritage remains valid, but broad tourist pull is limited.

Polygon-only pass found enough in-town visitor interest for a niche detour: Bennie Museum, Bathgate History Trail, Reconnect Regal Theatre, Kirkton Park and Bathgate Golf Club. Nearby countryside and out-of-polygon attractions were deliberately excluded.

Targeted curation confirmed in-polygon Bridge 19-40 canal boat trips, the community museum and the heritage art trail; Almondell and Calderwood is out of polygon and no longer counted. The remaining in-town offer still justifies a one-star niche detour.
Historic village evidence and old bridge context are not enough for a tourist rating; external attraction searches mostly point to Perth or Scone rather than Bridge of Earn itself.
Search results show local activities and village heritage rather than a coherent tourist-town draw.
Bridge, riverside and historic-townscape interest remain a niche detour rather than a planned-stop or destination draw.
